result.note: Tests the November 2025 rare earth permanent magnet programme and the composition of NdFeB magnets.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's push to manufacture rare earth permanent magnets, as of February 2026:
items: In November 2025, the government approved a USD 800 million programme to build an end-to-end rare earth permanent magnet manufacturing ecosystem.
Up to five private sector partners are to be selected through global competitive bidding.
India's consumption of these magnets is expected to double by 2040.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because India's consumption is expected to double by 2030, not 2040. The private partners will be supported by capital subsidies and production-linked incentives, and the Budget 2026-27 added dedicated rare earth corridors.
questions.source: In November 2025, New Delhi approved an USD 800 million programme to build an end-to-end rare earth permanent magnet manufacturing ecosystem.

questions.prompt: NdFeB permanent magnets, used in electric vehicles, wind turbines and modern weapons systems, are made of which elements?
questions.explain: NdFeB stands for neodymium-iron-boron. China controls 90% of global processing of these materials, which left India's defence and green energy supply chains exposed when China restricted shipments in 2025.
questions.source: Neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) magnets are inside every electric vehicle, wind turbine, and modern weapons system.
